name: Ponta Negra
tagline: The main beach district, under the Morro do Careca dune
description: Natal's tourist and expatriate centre, a long beach ending at the enormous Morro do Careca dune, with the hotels, restaurants, bars and most of the city's foreign residents along the seafront and the streets behind it. It is the safest and most serviced part of the city.
bestFor: Almost everyone arriving in Natal, for the services and the relative safety
pros: The best restaurants, bars and services in the city
Beach and promenade at the door
The most visible police presence and the safest streets
cons: Touristy, with the pricing that follows
Some streets behind the front are best avoided at night

name: Petropolis and Tirol
tagline: The established residential districts, where the city's professionals live
description: The traditional upper-middle-class neighbourhoods between the centre and the northern beaches, with tree-lined streets, apartment buildings, private schools and clinics. It is where Natal's professionals live, it has no beach and it is considerably calmer than Ponta Negra.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting a settled residential district rather than a tourist strip
pros: Quiet, shaded streets and good local services

name: Praia dos Artistas and Areia Preta
tagline: The city beaches below the fort, faded and central
description: The urban beaches just south of the Forte dos Reis Magos, once the fashionable stretch and now visibly past that, with older buildings, a seafront road and a mix of residents and cheaper hotels. It is central, cheap and requires more caution than Ponta Negra after dark.
bestFor: Budget stays wanting a central beach and accepting the trade-offs
pros: Beach and the historic fort within walking distance
Close to the city centre and its transport

name: Genipabu and the Northern Dunes (25 km north)
tagline: The dune landscape and the lagoons, across the river
description: North across the Potengi river, where the coast turns into a landscape of enormous shifting dunes and freshwater lagoons, with the buggy rides that Natal is known for and the village of Genipabu at the centre of it. Quiet, spectacular and a genuine drive from the city.
bestFor: Stays that want the dune landscape and do not need the city daily
pros: The dunes and lagoons immediately there
Far quieter than any city beach
cons: Forty minutes to an hour into Natal
Very limited services and no nightlife

name: Capim Macio and Neopolis
tagline: Between Ponta Negra and the university, newer and good value
description: The newer residential districts inland from Ponta Negra, with modern apartment blocks, supermarkets, the federal university nearby and rents noticeably below the beachfront. It is a fifteen-minute drive or a short bus ride to the beach and considerably more practical for a long stay.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting a newer flat at a rent that is not a beach rent
pros: Modern apartments well below Ponta Negra prices
Supermarkets, gyms and the university nearby
Ten to fifteen minutes from the beach
